title: The scalar localization of a linear triangulated category is triangulated
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\varpi\in R$, and let $\mathcal C$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] that is $R$-linear, with shift $[1]$ acting $R$-linearly on Hom modules. Equip the scalar localization $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] with the induced shift, and call a triangle of $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ distinguished if it is isomorphic, in $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$, to the image under the localization functor $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ of a distinguished triangle of $\mathcal C$. Then $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ is a triangulated category, and $Q$ is an exact functor (it commutes with the shifts and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles).

source.place: Proposition 13.5.6, Tag 05R6 (derived.tex line 1360), the triangulated structure on a localization at a multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated structure (Definition 13.5.1, Tag 05R2); to be applied to the saturated multiplicative system generated by the maps $\varpi^n\cdot\mathrm{id}_K$, whose localization is identified with $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$. The blueprint (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sf-operations/def-weil-rationalization-karoubi.md) uses this structure without stating it

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L=\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$. The scalar-category lemma supplies its composition, identities, the additive functor $Q$, and its induced $R[1/\varpi]$-linear shift commuting with $Q$. The old zero object and biproduct diagrams remain zero and biproduct diagrams: the zero Hom modules remain zero, and the equations for biproduct inclusions and projections are preserved by $Q$. Hence $\mathcal L$ is additive. By the natural tensor-localization isomorphism identify every Hom module of $\mathcal L$ with $\Hom_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)_\varpi$. Write its elements $f/\varpi^n$; composition is $(g/\varpi^m)\circ(f/\varpi^n)=(g\circ f)/\varpi^{m+n}$ and the shift is $f[1]/\varpi^n$. Equality $f/\varpi^n=g/\varpi^m$ means $\varpi^k(\varpi^mf-\varpi^ng)=0$ for some $k\ge0$. In particular $Q(f)=Q(g)$ means $\varpi^k(f-g)=0$ for some $k$.

source.place: Tag 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization; Tags 07JZ/07K0, module fractions; scalar-category construction in the blueprint rationalization display

proof.text: Define $S=\{s\mid Q(s)\text{ is invertible in }\mathcal L\}$. We verify the axioms of the cited multiplicative-system definition, using no triangulation on $\mathcal L$ yet. Every $\varpi^n\mathrm{id}_X$ belongs to $S$. If $s:X\to Y$ is in $S$, write $Q(s)^{-1}=h/\varpi^n$. The two inverse identities and the fraction equality criterion give exponents killing $hs-\varpi^n\mathrm{id}_X$ and $sh-\varpi^n\mathrm{id}_Y$. Choose a common exponent $k$, replace $h$ by $\varpi^kh$, and put $N=n+k$. Then in $\mathcal C$ itself $hs=\varpi^N\mathrm{id}_X$ and $sh=\varpi^N\mathrm{id}_Y$. MS1 follows since functors preserve identities and compositions. For MS4, if $Q(f)Q(g)$ and $Q(g)Q(h)$ are invertible, $Q(g)$ has both a left inverse and a right inverse, which agree, so $g\in S$. MS5 follows because the induced shift and its inverse are functors commuting with $Q$, and therefore preserve and reflect invertibility.

proof.text: For the first Ore square (MS2), given $t:X\to Z$ in $S$ and $g:X\to Y$, take $h:Z\to X$ with $ht=\varpi^N\mathrm{id}_X$ as in step 2. Set $s=\varpi^N\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $f=gh:Z\to Y$. Then $sg=ft$. For the other square, given $s:Y\to W$ in $S$ and $f:Z\to W$, choose $h:W\to Y$ with $sh=\varpi^N\mathrm{id}_W$, and set $t=\varpi^N\mathrm{id}_Z$, $g=hf$. Then $ft=sg$. Both new denominators belong to $S$. For MS3, either $ft=gt$ with $t\in S$, or $sf=sg$ with $s\in S$, implies $Q(f)=Q(g)$ by cancellation in $\mathcal L$. Choose $k$ with $\varpi^k(f-g)=0$. The denominator $\varpi^k\mathrm{id}_Y$ equalizes on the left and $\varpi^k\mathrm{id}_X$ equalizes on the right. Thus both calculus-of-fractions axioms hold.

proof.text: For each object $A$, applying the cited Hom exactness lemma to a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ and its rotations gives the exact five-term row $\Hom(A,X)\to\Hom(A,Y)\to\Hom(A,Z)\to\Hom(A,X[1])\to\Hom(A,Y[1])$. The rotations introduce signs on shifted arrows; replacing a homomorphism by its negative changes neither its kernel nor its image, so the displayed unsigned row is exact. Its maps are $R$-linear by bilinearity of composition. This row remains exact after localization, directly as follows: for an exact pair of linear maps $U\xrightarrow{a}V\xrightarrow{b}W$, if $b(y)/\varpi^n=0$, there is $k$ with $b(\varpi^ky)=0$. Choose $x$ with $a(x)=\varpi^ky$; then $y/\varpi^n=a(x)/\varpi^{n+k}$. The reverse inclusion of image in kernel follows from $ba=0$. Applying this calculation at the three middle terms and the tensor-localization isomorphism gives an exact row of additive groups $\Hom_{\mathcal L}(A,X)\to\Hom_{\mathcal L}(A,Y)\to\Hom_{\mathcal L}(A,Z)\to\Hom_{\mathcal L}(A,X[1])\to\Hom_{\mathcal L}(A,Y[1])$.

proof.text: For MS6, let two distinguished triangles and a commuting square $(s,s')$ with $s,s'\in S$ be given. TR3 in $\mathcal C$ completes the square to a triangle morphism $(s,s',c)$. Apply the rows of step 4 for each $A$. The vertical maps on the first, second, fourth and fifth terms are postcomposition by $Q(s),Q(s'),Q(s[1]),Q(s'[1])$, all invertible by step 2. The rows and vertical maps form a commutative diagram: its first three squares are the three equations of the triangle morphism after postcomposition, and the last is the shift of its first equation. The category of additive abelian groups satisfies [def-sp-abelian] directly: it has pointwise addition on homomorphisms, the trivial group and finite products as biproducts, subgroup kernels and quotient cokernels; monomorphisms are injective (test maps from $\mathbf Z$) and hence kernels of their quotient maps, while epimorphisms are surjective (test the quotient by the image) and hence cokernels of their kernel inclusions. The five lemma in this abelian category implies that postcomposition by $Q(c)$ is bijective on $\Hom_{\mathcal L}(A,Z)$ for every $A$. Taking $A=Z'$ supplies $r:Z'\to Z$ with $Q(c)r=\mathrm{id}_{Z'}$. Taking $A=Z$ and using injectivity on Hom shows $rQ(c)=\mathrm{id}_Z$, since postcomposing both $rQ(c)$ and $\mathrm{id}_Z$ with $Q(c)$ gives $Q(c)$. Thus $c\in S$. This proves MS6, so the saturated multiplicative system $S$ is compatible with triangulation.

proof.text: We now check that the concrete $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal L$ is a localization at $S$ in the universal-property sense of the cited definition. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ be any functor inverting $S$, with no additivity assumption on $F$ or $\mathcal B$. Put $d_X=F(\varpi\mathrm{id}_X)$, an automorphism, and define $\overline F(X)=F(X)$ and $\overline F(f/\varpi^n)=F(f)d_X^{-n}$. Naturality of scalar identities, $(\varpi\mathrm{id}_Y)f=f(\varpi\mathrm{id}_X)$, gives $d_YF(f)=F(f)d_X$. If $f/\varpi^n=g/\varpi^m$, the fraction criterion gives the equality of arrows $(\varpi^{k+m}\mathrm{id}_Y)f=(\varpi^{k+n}\mathrm{id}_Y)g$ in $\mathcal C$. Applying $F$ and canceling the invertible powers of $d_Y$ proves equality of the proposed images. The same commuting identity gives $\overline F(g/\varpi^m)\overline F(f/\varpi^n)=F(gf)d_X^{-(m+n)}$, and identities are preserved. Thus $\overline F$ is a functor extending $F$. It is unique because $f/\varpi^n=Q(f)Q(\varpi^n\mathrm{id}_X)^{-1}$. A natural transformation between two such $F$'s extends with the same object components: naturality for scalar identities gives naturality for their inverses, and hence for each displayed fraction. Its extension is unique since $Q$ is the identity on objects. Conversely restriction of functors and transformations along $Q$ inverts $S$ by its definition. This proves both required bijections.

proof.text: Apply the triangulated-localization theorem to $\mathcal C$, the compatible multiplicative system $S$ of steps 2--5, and its concrete localization $Q$ verified in step 6. Its induced shift is the shift of step 1: on every fraction both shifts send $f/\varpi^n$ to $f[1]/\varpi^n$. The theorem declares precisely the triangles isomorphic to localization images distinguished, namely the specified class of triangles of $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ isomorphic to $Q$-images of distinguished triangles of $\mathcal C$. It supplies the triangulated structure, including TR4, and exactness of $Q$. Therefore the claimed raw scalar localization, with no idempotent completion or extra hypotheses on $R$ or $\varpi$, is triangulated and $Q$ is exact.
